defects.defect: The outbound gate and the web helper contradict each other. The gate sets host lists (firewall: 'the gateway to its model, search and weather hosts'; proxy: 'an allowlist of model and connector hosts') and passes only when 'one request to an unlisted host' is refused 'through the path page fetches will actually take'. The helper built in the next phase has to fetch any public address. The installed docs say a configured proxy carries the gateway's own fetch and HTTP clients (security/network-proxy.md, 'How routing works'), and F019's own record says that once the helper has page fetch the proxy 'can deny private ranges and named hosts and nothing more' and that the deny-by-default firewall 'would have to allow that traffic'. So whichever route page fetches take, that route cannot hold a host list, and the gate as worded cannot pass with the helper working. The route is left to be 'settled when the plan is written', so the gate's 7 hours and 13 steps cannot be counted yet.
defects.fix: Settle the route in this definition and reword the gate: on the page-fetch path public hosts are allowed, and a home-network address, a redirect to one and a name that resolves to one are refused after the name is resolved. Host lists apply only to programs that never fetch pages (the mail connector, the alert senders, the backup), and the unlisted-host refusal is shown from the mail connector. Add one line for Tony's sign-off: after wave B neither the firewall nor the proxy holds the gateway program to a host list.

defects.defect: Counted from the item records, wave A in the form the definition draws (Tony's inbox, the coded check and the lookup) is about 26.5 hours and 53 steps, not 23.5 and 48, which is over one plan. The definition counts three places light: the scheduler switches with T3 plus a first firewall install on a Mac with two users is about 3.25 hours, not 2.5; the reader phase is about 7.5 hours and 13 steps, not 6 and 11 (key, generator, connector, T2, T5, the coded check, retention, and an eval-only copy whose test mailbox nothing provides); the jobs script and the morning text with three digests read against the inbox is about 3.75 hours, not 3. On this count about 21.5 hours are used when the lookup phase is reached, so the definition's own rule (over 20 hours) sends the lookup to wave B. Wave A then fits at about 24.5 hours and 49 steps with no slack, and the lookup, which the summary presents as part of wave A, is in practice the first phase of wave B.
defects.fix: State the lookup as outside wave A's budget, the way Jordan's inbox already is, and say that opening wave B with it is the expected case. If Tony wants the lookup inside wave A for certain, ask him in the first phase to choose between it and the coded check (S1), because by this count the two do not both fit.

defects.defect: Wave B's size (21 hours, 42 steps) leaves out its own second phase. Wave A's rules can send it the lookup (2 h), Jordan's inbox (1.5 h) and the envelope (1.5 h): 26 hours and 53 steps on the definition's own figures, and a total is given only for Jordan's inbox alone. My count of wave B with nothing carried over is already about 23.5 hours and 48 steps, because the gate is nearer 8.5 hours than 7 (blocking every program by default on a Mac that the admin account also works on, and a proxy that has to be built and run in report mode first). With the lookup carried over, which the wave A count above makes the expected case, wave B is about 25.75 hours and 52 steps. The day-out and weather phases 'can move' to wave C, but no rule says when, and wave C then stands at about 25 hours against its own ceiling of 22.
defects.fix: Give wave B's size with everything carried over, and add a rule like wave A's: if more than 2 hours arrive from wave A, the day out opens wave C; if more than 3.5, hourly weather goes with it. State in wave C which phase gives way when they arrive (next defect).

defects.defect: Wave C stays under its ceiling by a rule that ends in 'a phase that does not fit waits for the next plan', and there is no next plan among the waves. With every main answer yes it is about 22 hours and 45 steps on my count. Add the plugin if wave A went without it (1.5 h) and the day out and weather if they slid from wave B (3 h) and it is about 26.5. So in the all-yes case one or two phases listed in wave C end up in no wave while their ids still count as placed.
defects.fix: Name the order in which wave C's phases give way (for example: 'email me this' is never added on top, then the evening text, then the day out), and say that a phase dropped this way moves to the 'not in a wave yet' list with that reason.

defects.defect: T1's own text says the day-8 result decides the connector 'before the rest of the mail step is built'. Here the firewall rule and the whole reader phase (the connector server, its tool filter, T2 and the Gmail-tool turn of T5) are built during the wait, and only the schedule is held back. If the day-8 search fails and Tony picks a different connector, about 3 hours of that work is redone.
defects.fix: Say so in the reader phase: name the steps that would be redone and have Tony accept building them before day 8. Or have Tony do the Google project and sign-in a week before the first working session, so day 8 falls before the reader phase.

defects.defect: The reader phase needs 'an eval-only copy of the reader with a test mailbox', and the phase checks and the exit test lean on eval-only copies, but no phase provides the mailbox. It is either a second Google account with its own read-only sign-in (one more approval by hand) or a small stand-in server with the same tool names. Neither is in the list of sign-ins or in the hours.
defects.fix: Name which it is. If a real account, add its sign-in to the Google sign-in phase on day one; if a stand-in, add it as a step of the reader phase. About 1 hour either way (counted in my size for wave A).

defects.defect: The exit test passes only 'with the school lines first', but its three planted mails (hidden instructions, a false deadline, a medical subject) include no school mail, so on a morning with no real school mail the school half of the goal is not shown. The goal sentence also promises the lookup and Jordan's text, while the exit test says it depends on neither.
defects.fix: Add a fourth planted mail written as a school notice with a date. Reword the goal so the lookup and Jordan's text read as 'if built'.

defects.defect: The first text Happy ever sends by itself, from an agent that is not the one bound to Tony's handle, is first tried in the morning-text phase, after about 14 hours of build. M1's sign-off records that iMessage replies needed a workaround on this version. T3's throwaway job tests listing, updating and the failure alert, not delivery. T3 also has no named fallback if the deploy path cannot reach the scheduler, although the notes say every test's fallback is named in its phase.
defects.fix: Have T3's throwaway job announce one fixed line to Tony from a tool-less agent other than his own, in the scheduler phase. Name T3's fallback (the jobs script run by hand in the happy session, as M1 did for plugin installs).

defects.defect: If Tony answers Q8 part 1 with 'wait' (the review's default), the wave is built in full and then cannot close until OpenAI approves, with no bound. The definition says so but gives the plan no rule for it, and no phase checks that the Zero Data Retention application has actually been filed.
defects.fix: Add to the first phase: the application is filed and its date written down. State the rule for 'wait': the plan pauses after the reader phase with nothing scheduled, and its last two phases run when the approval arrives or Tony says go ahead.

defects.defect: The gate includes 'OpenClaw's secret egress proxy switched on'. In the installed docs (gateway/secrets/secret-store-and-egress.md) that proxy protects secrets kept in OpenClaw's shared store when an agent runs commands on the gateway. No Happy agent can run commands and the keys are in the Keychain, not that store, so the step has nothing to act on and no 'done when' check.
defects.fix: List it with the roadmap lines recorded as not carried (as the browser network rules are), with this reason, for Tony's sign-off.

defects.defect: The exit test covers a web question and a planted PDF from Tony's phone. It does not touch hourly weather, the day out, a photo or Jordan's agent, all of which are in the goal ('a parent can ...'). It also needs a public page that carries planted instructions without saying where that page lives or who puts it there.
defects.fix: Add to the same sitting, for whichever were built: one hourly rain question, one day-out request, one photo, and one web question from Jordan's phone. Say whether the planted page is one Tony publishes or the recorded page on the eval-only copy.

defects.defect: Waves B and C do not list the steps only Tony can do, or their fixed waits, as wave A does. In B: the helper's new capped key, the firewall's prompts, building the proxy, a report-mode period before enforcing, and 'Jordan's after a day'. In C: each parent's calendar sign-in on Google's screen, the sending account for 'email me this', typing the family facts, and an exit test that spans two days.
defects.fix: Add a 'by hand' line and the minimum number of calendar days to wave B and to wave C.

defects.defect: T7 has to be sent from iMessage, so for that test the scheduling tool must sit on an agent Tony's handle reaches, before any rule exists. The same phase says 'No tool is granted to a real agent in this phase.'
defects.fix: Say which agent carries the tool for T7, that the grant is made with script triggers off, and that it is removed in the same sitting before the rule is written.

defects.defect: F041 is listed as unconditional, but its build rests on T6 passing. If T6 fails, the only design left is the card's own (a read-write workspace and a write check), which reverses two signed-off settings and adds about 2.5 hours; no fallback is named. With Q6, Q4 and Q2 all answered no, wave C would then end with nothing a parent would notice.
defects.fix: Name the fallback for a failed T6 and its hours, and say it needs Tony's yes because it changes signed-off settings.

defects.defect: When the calendar phases are built, the exit test adds a calendar question and a planted event, but not the evening text arriving by itself at its hour, which is the part a parent would notice. 'Remember this' is promised for both parents; the exit test checks only that Jordan's agent cannot find Tony's fact.
defects.fix: Add to the exit test: the evening text arrived by itself at the named hour, and Jordan saves and recalls one harmless fact of her own.

defects.defect: The note that waves B and C can swap does not cover 'email me this'. The roadmap puts the send-to-owner test in the same gate as blocking every program by default and the proxy, and wave B builds that gate.
defects.fix: Add to the swap note: if wave C runs before wave B, 'email me this' waits for wave B's gate.

size.basis: My estimate from the item records, not a measurement, at about M1's rate (49 steps for about 20 hours, with a 3-hour exit gate). Simplified form (S6, S9, S14), Tony's inbox, coded check and lookup both built. Get ready with T8 and a backup: 1.75 h, 5 steps. Google project, gog, sign-in and T1 day one (G015's prerequisites): 3.25 h, 7 steps. G003 (three switches, job-list line, T3, later the jobs script): 2.25 h, 5 steps. Firewall, one rule (the gate for G015): 2 h, 4 steps. G015 reader (rated L): 7.5 h, 13 steps, of which the coded check with T5 is 2.5 h. F051 as the school lines in the 07:00 job, planted mails, day-8 check, three digests read: 2.75 h, 5 steps. G008 as one daily sign-in check: 1 h, 2 steps. G005, CRT-04 and CRT-05 as paper: 1 h, 3 steps. G015 lookup with T4: 2.25 h, 4 steps. Exit gate: 3 h, 5 steps. Total about 26.75 h and 53 steps, which does not fit. It fits one plan at about 24.5 h and 49 steps once the lookup slides to wave B by the definition's own rule, or at about 24.25 h without the coded check (S1 taken or T5 fails), or about 22 h and 45 steps without both. Jordan's inbox adds about 1.75 h and 4 steps; the envelope with T10 adds 1.5 h and 3 steps. As the cards are written (without S6, S9, S14) it is over 40 hours, two plans; I did not recount the definition's 41. Fixed wait: day 8 of the sign-in, so it cannot close before day nine.

My estimate, same method. Simplified form (S7, S15, the small day out), proxy built, nothing carried over from wave A. Get ready with a backup: 1.25 h, 4 steps. Outbound gate, 8.5 h and 17 steps: blocking every program by default 2.5 h, proxy 3.5 h, secret proxy switch and plugin allowlist 0.75 h, MAC-04 1 h (rated S, config and posture lines), re-checks 0.75 h. F019 with T4, four planted cases and the seeded-mail re-run: 5.5 h, 11 steps. F002 as one switch and one planted-file test: 2.25 h, 5 steps. F083 hourly only (rated S): 1.25 h, 2 steps. F028 small form (card rated L; as written about 7 h): 1.75 h, 4 steps. Exit gate: 3 h, 5 steps. Total about 23.5 h and 48 steps: fits, near the top. It stops fitting with what wave A can send it: with the lookup about 25.75 h and 52 steps; with Jordan's inbox as well about 27.5 h and 56; with the envelope too about 29 h. It fits again if the day out (and then hourly weather) move to wave C. If Tony waives the proxy, about 3.5 h less. With the privacy-gate plugin (S7 declined) about 2.5 h more. The gate hours are provisional until the page-fetch route is settled (first defect).

My estimate, same method. Simplified form (S5, S8, S10, S11 and the one-plugin shape of S1), every main answer yes, no 'email me this', nothing slid in from wave B. Get ready with a backup: 1.25 h, 4 steps. T7, T5 again, the reminder rule and the five-way recipient test: 3.25 h, 6 steps. F042 typed facts (rated S): 1.25 h, 3 steps. F041 with T6, settings for both parents and the memory-search canaries: 4.75 h, 9 steps. F007: 2.75 h, 6 steps. F010 as a standing rule and one test: 1 h, 2 steps. F009 with the calendar half of T2: 3.25 h, 7 steps. F014 as one evening text: 1.75 h, 3 steps. Exit gate over two days: 3 h, 5 steps. Total about 22.25 h and 45 steps: fits. F049 is about 4.75 h and 9 steps and fits only in place of the calendar phases or the reminder phases, as the definition says. Add 1.5 h if the plugin is first created here, and about 3 h if the day out and weather arrive from wave B: then about 25 to 26.5 h, and a phase has to leave (fourth defect). Smallest version (typed facts, notes, the file-write turn of T5): about 10.75 h and 22 steps. As the cards are written about 40 hours by the definition's count, which I did not recount.
